comparator.name: Business Administration (Bedrijfskunde)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted SBE OER 2026–27, annex VII official programme chart version 19 February 2026; checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: Strategy and Organisation (Strategie en Organisatie) specialisation
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted programme chart gives 60 compulsory EC in year one (ten 6-EC modules); 48 compulsory EC and two separate 6-EC restricted choices in year two (the first-listed Accounting II in period four, Entrepreneurship in period five); and a third year with 30 EC genuinely open minor space, 6 EC Ethics, two 6-EC courses in one formally selected specialisation, and a 12-EC thesis tied to that specialisation. The Strategy and Organisation specialisation has Foundations of Strategic Management and Strategic Management from a Practice Perspective. It is selected as the most general business-management specialisation, independently of UCR fit; more narrowly functional routes such as Accounting, Finance and Marketing are not mixed in. Zero-credit research participation and personal/professional-development items are not added to the 180 EC. No optional alternative choice is presented as compulsory for all students.
components: One of four restricted 6-EC period-four choices (Accounting II, Samenleving en Bedrijf, Supply Chain Management II, Technologie en Innovatiemanagement); first listed chosen.
One of three restricted 6-EC period-five choices (Ondernemerschap, Financieel Management II, Marketing II); first listed chosen.
Genuinely open 30-EC third-year academic minor or exchange space; no elective courses are invented.
Strategic Management from a Practice Perspective
Required 12-EC bachelor thesis on the selected Strategy and Organisation specialisation.

alternatives.label: Business strategy, markets and organisational decisions
alternatives.concept: Combines accounting and finance, economics, marketing, strategy, management and leadership with quantitative analysis of business decisions. Digital change and AI are studied as business conditions, while the curriculum is broader than the comparator’s Strategy and Organisation specialisation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme spans the functional areas of business and emphasises strategy, markets and organisational decisions without claiming to be solely a finance or marketing major.
progression: First-year entrepreneurship, business research and relevant psychology or programming precede upper-level finance, strategy, AI or organisational research. Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability were checked against the enriched workbook; advisory sequencing has been reviewed.

alternatives.label: Digital business, AI and new ventures
alternatives.concept: Organises business study around new ventures, product development and digital transformation, adding programming, databases, algorithms and machine learning to economics, marketing, management and business research. The programme asks how firms use AI and digital information to develop new products and models.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set includes entrepreneurship and marketing alongside several computing and AI courses, which materially define this programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses differ from the balanced route, including databases, mathematical methods, AI ethics, deep learning, optimisation and algorithm design in place of a larger business-law, economics and negotiation component; this changes the tools and type of strategic problem the student studies.
progression: First-year entrepreneurship, business research and relevant psychology or programming precede upper-level finance, strategy, AI or organisational research. Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability were checked against the enriched workbook; advisory sequencing has been reviewed.

alternatives.label: People, leadership and organisational change
alternatives.concept: Studies firms through employee behaviour, social psychology, leadership, organisational culture and management advice, retaining economics, strategy and marketing as business context. Qualitative and experimental methods support research into workplace problems and strategic change.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed course set puts leadership, organisational behaviour and research into employee and team processes at its centre.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the closest route, this curriculum adds sociology, social psychology, qualitative and experimental research, and focuses the business courses on leadership and organisational change; it reduces finance and AI methods rather than merely renaming a shared programme.
progression: First-year entrepreneurship, business research and relevant psychology or programming precede upper-level finance, strategy, AI or organisational research. Formal prerequisites and Fall 2026–Spring 2029 availability were checked against the enriched workbook; advisory sequencing has been reviewed.

routeSelection.route: Strategy and Organisation (Strategie en Organisatie) specialisation
routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized Bedrijfskunde target requires one of the formally listed year-three specialisations to be instantiated. Strategy and Organisation is the broadest management/organisational strategy direction rather than a narrow functional area; the two named 6-EC units and linked 12-EC thesis are taken together from annex VII of the adopted 2026–27 OER. This academic representation was chosen before comparing UCR courses.

selection.assessment: The first curriculum covers broad business functions, the second adds technical digital-business and AI work, and the third concentrates on organisational change and people. All three concepts follow target-specific interests, produce materially different 24-course selections, and meet the pairwise four-course floor. Transport/supply-chain management is a separate supported interest but UCR has no dedicated logistics sequence to support a further 24-course direction; in any event three defensible options already meet the maximum.

notes.text: VU combines prescribed business functions and methods with a third-year Strategy and Organisation specialisation, a 12-EC thesis and a 30-EC open minor. UCR offers business, economics, leadership, research and digital courses in more flexible combinations, without reproducing the VU supply-chain sequence, advanced accounting choice or specialisation thesis.
